uc1.title: Use case 1 — Temporal dynamics
uc1.alt: Use case 1 — Temporal dynamics: annual growth of light
uc1.caption: Between 2014 and 2025, night-time light in South Africa changed by +2.1% per year (95% CI: +0.6% to +3.0%). Over the last 12 months, the seasonally adjusted level is +3.0% relative to the previous 12 months. (confidence high: significant trend (p < 0.01; n = 12))
uc1.source: VIIRS DNB monthly (VCMSLCFG) · NOAA/EOG · Google Earth Engine

uc3.title: Use case 3 — Lights and GDP
uc3.alt: Use case 3 — Lights and GDP: light–GDP elasticity
uc3.caption: The elasticity of light with respect to real GDP is 1.96 in levels (95% CI: −0.19 to 4.11, R² = 0.36, 12 years) and −0.27 in growth rates (CI: −0.98 to 0.45). Out of sample, light growth tracks GDP growth with a correlation of −0.54 (mean absolute error: 1.7 percentage points of growth). (confidence medium: n = 12, significant but wide CI (4.31))

uc4.title: Use case 4 — Economic shocks
uc4.alt: Use case 4 — Economic shocks: shock trough
uc4.caption: The most pronounced shock in the seasonally adjusted series is “COVID-19”: trough of -10.4% (09/2020), return to the pre-shock level after 7 months. (confidence low: trough compared with pre-shock month-to-month variability)
uc4.source: VIIRS DNB monthly (VCMSLCFG) · NOAA/EOG · Google Earth Engine

uc6.title: Use case 6 — Industrial zones
uc6.alt: Use case 6 — Industrial zones: industrial clusters
uc6.caption: 400 industrial clusters detected from concordant satellite signals: 40 heavy industry, 77 business parks & logistics, 221 oil & gas sites and 62 isolated sites to verify. They emit 22.3% of national light (latest year); their light changes by -1.4% per year. Gauteng has the most industrial activity. (confidence low: no reference list available to validate the detection)
